voice.stance: The essayist analyst. LOGOS is the one language that writes in dense prose: full sentences that argue, in the tradition of the printed chartbook. The title states a claim, the paragraph proves it, the source sits beside it. Causal connectives are the product here, because the reader came for the because.
voice.hedging: allowed when it states the confidence
voice.title_grammar: The claim as an assertion, with the cause in a subordinate clause.
voice.title_example: Freight cost peaked in March because the joints shipped by air

do.rule: Use causal connectives: because, despite, which explains.
do.why: Analysis without causality is a table read out loud.

do.rule: Cite the source next to the claim, never in an appendix.
do.why: The language's law is that sources stay visible; the prose obeys the same law.

do.rule: Keep exact figures where they carry the argument.
do.why: In a deep dive, 18.3% and about 18% are different claims.

dont.rule: Never flag your own findings as worth attention.
dont.why: "Interestingly" and "notably" ask the reader to be impressed. Show the anomaly instead.

dont.rule: No assertion without its evidence in the same breath.
dont.why: An unanchored claim breaks the core contract of this language.

dont.rule: No bullet fragments in body text.
dont.why: LOGOS argues in sentences. Fragments belong to KATA and NOROSHI.

contrast.generic: The data shows an interesting trend in freight volumes that is worth examining in more detail.
contrast.voiced: Freight volume fell 18% after April, when cable moved from air to sea (packing lists, weeks 14 to 22).
